answer: Per-identity sybil insurance makes every seat buy its own cover before it can earn. An underwriter backs each seat with 500 POA that goes to whoever later proves it a clone, and charges a premium priced to that risk. Quotes rise with similarity to seats already insured: a 50th seat sharing timing and phrasing with 49 others is quoted 20 times the first. So N fakes pay N steeply climbing premiums, and self-insuring fails because the underwriter's own bond is slashed too. An honest seat pays one modest premium, whether it grades a sonnet, schedules harbor berths or maps tundra thaw.
